title: Cửa Lò in July: when to be on the sand and when not to be
excerpt: July is the busiest month on the Nghệ An coast. Here is how the day runs, and which hours are worth getting up for.
body:
Cửa Lò fills from the last week of June. The beach has two good windows: before eight in the morning, when the fishing boats are still landing and the sand is cool, and after five in the afternoon when the heat goes out of it. Between those, the town eats and sleeps.

The fish market behind the beach road opens as the boats come in, around half past five. Buy there and a stall on the beach road will grill it for you by the kilo.

Rooms on the beach road cost roughly twice in July what they cost in October, and the good ones are gone by May. If your dates are fixed, book the room first and the trip around it.

title: Kim Liên with children: a half day that holds their attention
excerpt: Uncle Hồ's hometown is 18 km from Vinh and works best early, with a guide who talks to the children rather than over them.
body:
Kim Liên is two houses, a lotus pond and a set of village lanes, and it is quiet before nine. Go then. A guide from Nam Đàn will tell the story as a family story, which is the version children stay with.

There is shade along the lanes and almost none at the houses, so hats matter more than anything else you bring. The tea house on the road out is the natural end of the morning.

title: Pù Mát: what to pack for the river and the forest
excerpt: Two days in the park means one boat, one jeep and a night in a stilt house. Pack for all three.
body:
The boat from Phà Lài is open, so you will be in sun for two hours and then in forest shade. Long sleeves beat sunscreen on the water.

The stilt houses at Bản Nưa provide bedding and nets. What they do not provide is a torch, and the walk to the river at first light is before the generators come on.

The park permit is included in every operator's price here; if a listing does not say so, ask before you pay.

title: Thanh Chương tea islands: why it has to be dawn
excerpt: The tea hills photograph for about forty minutes a day. Here is which forty.
body:
The mist sits in the water between the tea islands until the sun clears the ridge, which in November is about a quarter past six. After seven it is a green hillside like any other.

That means leaving Vinh before five. Every operator running this trip knows it; one that offers a nine o'clock departure is selling you a different photograph.

The picking families work the rows from first light and are generally happy to be asked before being photographed.
